correctness.rationale: For each ell>=2 both source forests have 2ell vertices and 2ell-2 edges, with components of order >=ell-1, exactly meeting Spinoza-West Theorem 1.7. In T(X), classify a chosen s-vertex subset into a original vertices U and b chosen edge-vertices. Internal, crossing and external incident-edge choices are expressed by products of vertex-degree and induced-edge quantities of total incidence degree <=b; aggregating their exact joint incident-edge patterns uses at most a+b=s original vertices, recoverable by s-deck marginals. This proves the transfer lemma for s>=2; its application is at s=ell. For forests each triangle is precisely the unique triangle attached to one source edge; disjoint triangle sets correspond to source matchings. A perfect matching occurs in exactly one of the two source path forests (parity alternates with ell), so the tiling polynomials differ. T(X) has 4ell-2 vertices, making ell/(4ell-2)->1/4. Independent brute-force canonical induced-deck enumeration for ell=2,3,4 verified both source and expanded deck equality and the alternating perfect-matching distinction; this finite test corroborates, but does not establish, arbitrary ell.
residual_risks: Degree-moment deck-transfer reconstruction relies on retaining incidence coincidences for products of cut-edge choices; the proof explains these via witnesses involving at most s original vertices. Small exhaustive tests independently corroborated this nonstandard step.
The result proves a lower bound, not equality of the optimal reconstruction constant.
